course_name_original: Métodos Cuantitativos de Ingeniería de Organización

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity and critical reasoning.
Ability to organize and plan in the field of business, and other institutions and organizations.
Understand, model, analyze, and solve organizational problems in industrial and service companies using quantitative methods, optimization, validation, and simulation.
Know and apply the fundamentals and techniques for business organization and the design and management of production and logistics systems.
Understand the main regression models, the advantages and limitations of linear models, and identify, formulate and solve real problems of linear models and interpret their meaning.
Handle statistical packages for solving real problems.
Use forecasting methods to know future demand in advance.
Model and solve real problems of linear, integer and mixed programming related to the business system.
Model and solve real problems of transportation and distribution.

syllabus_topics: Enumerative methods: B&B and explicit enumeration

assessment_methods.method: Proposed assignments (individual work and lab attendance)

assessment_rules: The final grade is the sum of 75% from the theoretical and practical problems exam and 25% from proposed assignments. A total of 5 points out of 10 is required to pass the course, with no minimum grade in any section. Attendance to at least 5 out of 7 laboratory practicals is mandatory to consider the points obtained in the final assignment. Optional additional exercises can add up to one point to the final grade only if the student has obtained between 4 and 4.9 points, or more than 8.25 points. For extraordinary evaluations, the score from proposed assignments is retained and combined with the exam score and, if applicable, the optional exercises.
